explain.say: A contrail, short for condensation trail, is a line of cloud made by a plane. Burning jet fuel makes hot gas full of water vapour, along with tiny specks of soot.

explain.say: At cruising height the air is around minus 40 degrees Celsius or colder. The hot, moist exhaust cools within a second or two, and its water vapour condenses onto the soot specks.
The tiny droplets freeze straight away into ice crystals, which scatter sunlight and look white. It is the same way your breath makes a cloud on a cold morning.

explain.say: If the air up there is dry, the ice turns back into vapour and the trail vanishes in seconds. If the air is humid, the trail can last for hours and spread into thin, wispy cloud.

faq.a: Contrails are made of tiny ice crystals. Water vapour from burning jet fuel freezes onto soot specks in the very cold air behind the engines.
asks: Is the white trail from a plane smoke?

faq.a: The ice crystals scatter all colours of sunlight about equally, so the trail looks white, just like a cloud.

faq.q: Why do some contrails last longer than others?
faq.a: It depends on how humid the air is at that height. In dry air the ice quickly turns back to vapour and the trail vanishes; in moist air the ice survives and spreads into thin cloud.
asks: Why do some plane trails disappear quickly?

faq.q: Are contrails bad for the climate?
faq.a: Long-lasting contrails can trap heat, especially at night. Scientists estimate their warming effect may be as large as that of aviation's carbon dioxide, though it is less certain, and airlines are testing routes that avoid the humid layers where they form.

faq.q: Why don't planes leave contrails near the ground?
faq.a: Near the ground the air is usually too warm for the exhaust's water vapour to freeze, so it just disappears. Contrails usually form only in very cold air, high up.
asks: Why do low planes not make trails?

facts: Burning one kilogram of jet fuel produces about 1.2 kilograms of water.
Contrails generally form where the air is colder than about minus 40 degrees Celsius.
